title: Independent Locating-Dominating Sets in Pseudotrees
summary: An ILD-set in a connected graph is a subset $S$ of vertices such that it is both independent and locating-dominating. The independent locating-dominating number of a graph G is the minimum cardinality of an ILD-set set of $G$. A well-known fact is that any graph with girth at least 5 has an ILD-set, but that is not clear for graphs with girth 3 and 4. In this work, we prove that there are graphs with no ILD-sets for any order $n\geq 9$ and girth 4, also showing some sufficient conditions for a bipartite graph to contain an ILD-set.
